title: Smart tool loop: telemetry-driven termination sentinels and typed result injection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: multi-tool chains in streaming API flows currently surface two recurring issues: (1) unbounded recursion and accidental loops when tool results are re-injected back into the planner, and (2) incompatible result shapes when older SDK tool signatures are chained into new structured-output contracts. Both lead to increased latency, cost, and occasional corrupted responses in production.

Goal: design a unified runtime-side guard and compatibility layer that enforces per-request invocation budgets, provenance-aware result injection, typed result validation, and streaming-safe backpressure so that multi-tool chains remain predictable and observable while preserving streaming and function-calling UX.

Scope: runtime changes to the orchestrator and executor, API surface for tool adapters, telemetry events and metrics, e2e tests and a gradual rollout plan. This ticket focuses on the guard layer, the typed injection contract, and compatibility adapters for legacy tool signatures. Separate follow-ups will handle batching/quantization heuristics and Dedicated-specific policies.

Design summary: 1) Invocation budget: attach a per-request budget object that includes max_invocations (default 8), remaining_budget, max_depth (default 4), and a soft_budget that triggers warnings at 50% remaining. Budget is decremented on each tool call. Requests that exhaust budget return a structured fallback hint to the caller (see AC). 2) Termination sentinels: runtime injects a synthesized termination token into the stream metadata when budget is exhausted or a circular provenance pattern is detected. Consumer SDKs will stop further tool planning when they see the sentinel. 3) Provenance tagging: every tool result is annotated with a provenance header string (e.g., "prov:tool:translate:v3:invocation_id") and an invocation_trace array represented as a delimited string for downstream analysis. 4) Typed result injection: tool adapters must emit results in one of three canonical forms: text, json_object, or binary_blob. A lightweight schema contract (JSON Schema string enforced at runtime) is attached to function signatures; mismatches generate a validation_error event and trigger a compatibility adapter. 5) Compatibility layer: implement adapter registry to map legacy tool payloads to canonical forms using declarative mapping rules (field renames, path extraction, simple transforms). Adapters run in a sandbox and are rate-limited. 6) Streaming/backpressure: when streaming responses include repeated tool calls, the orchestrator buffers only necessary KV state and streams chunks with explicit backpressure signals (chunk_ack tokens). 7) Metrics and telemetry: emit events for invocation_start, invocation_end, budget_update, budget_exhausted, sentinel_emitted, validation_error, adapter_run, recursion_detected. Provide SLI thresholds and dashboards.

Tradeoffs considered: - Aggressive budget enforcement prevents runaway costs but may truncate valid complex plans; mitigated by canarying softer defaults and exposing per-customer knobs. - Runtime schema validation increases latency; mitigate by permitting asynchronous adapter runs and emitting partial streaming chunks with placeholders. - Compatibility adapters add complexity and potential security surface; mitigated by running adapters in sandboxed processes with limited syscall access and KMS-protected secrets.

Acceptance criteria: - Orchestrator enforces a default per-request max_invocations and max_depth and decrements budget on each tool call. - Termination sentinel appears in stream metadata and is consumable by SDKs. - Provenance headers are attached to 100% of tool results. - A JSON Schema validation path rejects mismatched tool results and triggers an adapter run. - Adapter registry can transform at least three legacy tool payload patterns into canonical json_object form. - Telemetry events are emitted and available in Console with charts for budget_exhausted and recursion_detected. - Unit and integration tests cover recursion scenarios, adapter transforms, and streaming client behavior.

Test plan: - Unit tests for budget decrement, sentinel emission, provenance tagging, and schema validation. - Integration tests that simulate nested tool chains and confirm the sentinel stops further planning. - Fuzz tests on legacy payloads to validate adapters and ensure no crashes. - Load tests to measure latency impact of validation and adapter runs with streaming enabled.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout with three phases: internal-only, opt-in beta for select customers, and gradual 10%->50%->100% traffic ramp. Monitor budget_exhausted and validation_error metrics during ramp.

Notes and links: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CORE/pages/Tool+Loop+Sentinel+Design (internal), relevant PRs: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8675 (adapter infra), monitoring dashboard: Console -> Streaming -> Tool Loop Safety.
